name: easing-curves
title: Easing curves compared
summary: Linear, ease-in (square), ease-out, smooth_step and smootherstep drawn over each other on one unit-square chart, each a pathExpression in t = a[0], with a legend.
prompt: Plot five easing curves from 0 to 1 on the same chart (linear, ease in, ease out, smoothstep, smootherstep) with a colour legend and the formula under each name.
teaches: Shape a 0..1 parameter with plain expressions: square(t) eases in, 1 - square(1 - t) eases out, smooth_step(t, 1, 0) and t*t*t*(t*(6*t - 15) + 10) ease both ends
Plot y = f(t) as a pathExpression with start 0, end 1 and a[0] as t, mapping it into the box with x = left + w * t and y = bottom - h * f(t)
Reuse one id per curve ("easeIn", "smooth"…) and draw it with drawPath after setting the stroke
pitfalls: smooth_step takes (value, max, min): smooth_step(t, 1, 0) is the usual smoothstep(0, 1, t). Not clamp's order
pathExpression without flags 4 (LINEAR) joins the samples with splines; 64 linear samples are enough for these curves, a straight line needs only count 2
The JSON parser has no smoothstep, mix or ease names: write the polynomial, and keep it under 32 RPN tokens

A canvas drawn at its header size (literal coordinates) runs off a narrower host and leaves a strip in a wider one: when the drawing is one composition (chart and legend, dial and readout), scale it as a whole with @fit = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H) and centre it with a translate

snippets.note: smooth_step(a[0], 1, 0): value first, then max, then min
smootherstep t³(t(6t − 15) + 10) as a 64-sample linear pathExpression

check.describe: Five curves from bottom-left to top-right: a grey diagonal, blue below it, green above it, yellow and red S-curves crossing at the centre, the red steeper. Resized, the chart and its legend are scaled as one (@fit = min(w / 360, h / 240)) and centred: smaller at 234 wide with the legend still beside the chart, centred at 1:1 in a 540 wide box.
